records.title: ‘Nobody showed up but me’: will Friendsgiving survive gen Z?
records.summary: A generation known for loneliness is putting their own spin on a millennial-made tradition that requires socializing It’s a TikTok scene straight out of a stress dream: two men stand in their freshly cleaned apartment, explaining how all but one of the people they invited to Friendsgiving flaked out at the last minute. There is a can of whipped cream on the table and a 6lb ham in the oven. According to the video, posted by pop-culture podcaster Jackson Strike, those who ditched were either tired, or sick, or had a difficult day at work. More than 1.5 million people liked the video and many flooded to the comments section to express their disappointment at what they saw as an epidemic of antisocial behavior. “Everyone wants a village until they have to be a villager,” one user wrote. “Time to get new friends,” quipped another. My older brother Abdullah had taught it to me when I was nine: lie down on a speed bump, legs long and both arms outstretched by your ears, making your body a long pencil. I was in the wrong position that day – it was so hot that the backs of my shins seared when they touched the road, so I had to bend my knees. Nadia wasn’t allowed to have her legs exposed anymore, so her linen trousers protected her. The game was intuitive – when you hear a car coming, roll down the slope and run away as fast you can. records.title: Spain has been hit hard by the climate crisis. Why are politicians saying so little about it before the election?
records.summary: Wildfires and floods can do little to move climate change up voters’ list of priorities, experts say Beneath the blackened branches of a pine tree that rises high above a landscape of scorched hillsides and the odd charred and ruined house, two older men address the obvious. Four months after one of the summer’s many wildfires threatened to devour the hamlet of El Morro , an hour west of Madrid, local people are still counting the cost and awaiting compensation. “Look at that house,” said Esteban Pérez, pointing to one of the properties that did not make it through July’s flames. “Everything inside is scorched, completely destroyed. It is widely agreed that the choice of its next secretary general is critical – perhaps even existential. Unfortunately, that’s where agreement ends. Under the opaque selection system, security council members are privately polled on their views of each candidate. A “discourage” vote from one of the five permanent members is diplomacy-speak for a veto. Only when a consensus emerges does the general assembly get a say on the candidate. records.title: Bill Bailey is an absolute master of musical mischief – this crowd hangs on every twang
records.summary: SEC Armadillo, Glasgow The comedian’s new concoction, Vaudevillean, mixes offbeat historical diversions, topical gags and virtuoso musical flights with warmth and absurdity Is any act ever really too niche for stardom? What could be more leftfield, after all, than Bill Bailey’s animated pop-musicology, with demonstrations on the Swedish nyckelharpa and the one-stringed Indian lute? But tonight he has yet another arena crowd hanging on his every strum, drumbeat and twang. Nothing need be niche, perhaps, if communicated with the open-hearted curiosity and passion Bailey brings to his esoteric interests. Add a flair for improbable juxtaposition, and a sense of humour that dusts curmudgeonliness with surrealism, and you’ve got a concoction that thousands-strong audiences find difficult to resist. The 61-year-old’s current show is called Vaudevillean, and gestures are made towards justifying that title, with reference to the French poet Olivier Basselin and the 1453 battle of Castillon. (You don’t get this with Michael McIntyre.) Like vaudeville, the show certainly has variety to recommend it. But really, this offering differs little from many a previous Bailey outing , and finds our host again following his nose from one unlikely musical experiment to another, via nuggets of topical standup and anecdotes from his storied life. Inflation rose in 16 member states in October, fell in nine and held steady in two. records.title: The Labour party has lost the plot on net zero | Letters
records.summary: Raymond T Pierrehumbert and Dr Lynne Jones respond to an article by the energy secretary, Miatta Fahnbulleh Watching Miatta Fahnbulleh, the secretary of state for energy security and net zero, forced to defend the government’s retreat from net zero ( Where do people want to see Britain’s climate action plan working? On their own doorstep, 17 November ) was painfully reminiscent of the way in which Colin Powell, a former US secretary of state and an honourable man, was forced to defend George W Bush’s claims justifying the disastrous Iraq war. Fahnbulleh states that people need to see the benefits of net zero on their doorstep – meaning jobs, cost of living and warm homes. But in fact the policies of this government mark a retreat of all of these “doorstep” benefits. Andy Burnham has slashed heat pump subsidies , which means more vulnerability of homes to heating price shocks from international affairs spiking fossil gas prices; it also means fewer warm homes and jobs in the heat pump manufacturing and installation industry. Continue reading...

records.title: The British Library is wrong to repurpose its reading rooms | Letters
records.summary: To distort what was actually a reduction in supply into a reduction in demand and then use it as ‘evidence’ is unworthy of our world-class research institution, says Marcia Saunders After a cyber-attack in 2023 , which Ciaran Martin, a former CEO of the National Cyber Security Centre, described as “ one of the worst cyber incidents in British history ”, use of the British Library’s reading rooms fell dramatically ( British Library to outsource security and ‘repurpose’ reading rooms as business spaces, 20 November ). Throughout 2024-25, services were heavily affected, including archives, manuscripts, books and online journal articles. All readers’ tickets were suspended and initially were reissued for limited periods of time. It should surprise no one that use of the reading rooms fell off. Only last month was access to the UK web archive (partially) restored. Continue reading...

records.title: NI Water Works - Cornagrade Road Enniskillen 3 Aug
records.summary: Essential Water Infrastructure Improvement Work gets underway – Cornagrade Road, Enniskillen NI Water is set to commence an upgrade of the water infrastructure on Cornagrade Road, Enniskillen in early August for approximately 6 weeks. The work will see around 400m of new watermain being laid along Cornagrade Road, starting at Cherrymount Roundabout on Monday 3 rd August and progressing as far as the second entrance to Kilmacormick Road. To facilitate the laying of this new watermain, a lane closure will be in place around each working area and signage will be in place. Working areas will be kept as short as possible (around 100m) with temporary traffic lights in place to manage the flow of traffic. Access to residential and business properties on and adjacent to Cornagrade Road will be available at all times, although parking spaces within the working area will be affected for a short period of time while the pipelaying passes. Any bus stop located within a working area will be temporarily relocated.

methodology.reliability: A official primary source/catalogue; B established newsroom or independent research; C specialist, advocacy or aggregator; D alternative commentary; E unverified social/community; U unclassified. Grade describes source class, not the truth of a specific claim.
methodology.confidence: Claim confidence is left unassessed unless an upstream collector supplies a numeric value. Source grade is not claim confidence.
methodology.corroboration: The six views reuse the existing archive. Similar stories, repeated posts, syndicated copy or multiple outlets quoting one origin are not independent corroboration. A human must inspect provenance.
methodology.geolocation: Location is shown only when supplied by the source or upstream archive. No location is inferred from a headline.
methodology.limits: This is open-source situational awareness, not intelligence agency coverage, an emergency warning service, a live market terminal or a verified threat assessment.
